 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, challenging the impugned judgment and award dated January 3, 2018, passed in MVC No.773/2015 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Holalkere.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Holalkere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking just and proper compensation for injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on November 8, 2014,
allegedly due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.
The appellant-Insurance Company contended that the motorcycle was insured under the policy and had been falsely implicated to claim compensation.

The Tribunal, after evaluating the evidence on record, concluded that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle insured by the Insurance Company and awarded compensation of Rs.2,11,500/- with interest at 6% per annum.
Taking exception to this decision, the appellant-Insurance Company has filed this appeal.

3. The learned counsel for the appellant argues that the alleged accident took place on November 8,
2014, but the First Information Report (FIR) was lodged on December 11, 2014, without providing a plausible explanation for the delay.
Furthermore, the pillion rider was not examined to substantiate that the claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
The Medico-Legal Case (MLC) register issued by the hospital where the claimant received treatment indicated that the injuries were due to NC: 2024:KHC:22057 a self-fall and slip from the motorcycle.
Therefore, in the absence of cogent evidence to substantiate that the claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, the impugned award passed by the Tribunal is not legally sustainable.

4. In contrast, the learned counsel for the claimant contends that the evidence of the claimant, the charge sheet material, and the wound certificate clearly establish that the claimant sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.
The Tribunal, after appreciating the evidence, rightly passed the impugned judgment, which does not warrant any interference.

sentences.text: Having considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and reviewed the Trial Court Records, it is clear that the alleged accident occurred on November 8, 2014, and the FIR was lodged on December 11, 2014, without a plausible explanation for the delay.

Although the claimant alleged that the accident occurred while he was riding his motorcycle with a pillion rider,
the pillion rider was not examined to corroborate that the claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
6. The wound certificate indicated that the claimant sustained injuries, and the Police charge sheeted the rider of the offending motorcycle for rash and negligent riding.
However, this alone does not establish that the motorcycle insured by the appellant was involved in the accident.
The MLC register issued by NC: 2024:KHC:22057 the hospital where the claimant was treated indicated that the injuries were due to a self-fall and slip from the motorcycle.

7. The Tribunal, ignoring these material aspects, concluded that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle insured by the appellant-Insurance Company.
This finding is erroneous.
8. The claimant failed to establish that he sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending motorcycle covered under the policy insured by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation, is not maintainable.
9. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment and award is set aside, and the claim petition is dismissed.
The statutory amount in deposit, as well as the amount deposited before this Court, shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal and released in favor of the appellant-Insurance Company.
